Subject: Post-call: connection multiplexing & throughput — action items

Hi Lina —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we're aligned: 

Summary
- FastLane's primary concern: peak parallelism during batch ingestion windows (300–500 parallel generation requests for short bursts, sustained ~150 concurrent requests during business hours).
- Latency target: 95th percentile < 350ms for short-completion prompts, streaming sessions allowed for longer-running transforms.
- You're interested in connection pooling + multiplexing rather than opening thousands of sockets.

Action items (owners & timing)
1) FastLane to share a short sample of request size distribution and expected burst pattern (Lina) — deliver by Wed 1/14.
2) Redwood to map the sample to an initial conn-pool configuration and a suggested rate-limit/burst profile; include expected token-cost deltas and a conservative SLO projection (Karthik) — deliver by Fri 1/16.
3) Marissa to provide a quick note on credits/introductory burst allowances we can offer for the pilot (Marissa) — deliver by Thu 1/15.
4) Ben to sketch a fallback model mapping (higher-latency cheaper variant) for graceful degradation if capacity saturates (Ben) — deliver by Mon 1/19.

Attachments: I attached the template spreadsheet we discussed (conn_requirements.xlsx) — please fill the simple columns for distribution of short/medium/long prompts and expected session lengths.

If that captures things, I'll follow up with the config doc and an initial ratecard mapping. Thanks again — excited to get a pilot running.

Best,
Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik — this is perfect and matches our notes. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- The 300–500 parallel number is for our nightly enrichment window (approx 30–45 mins). During the day most spikes are in the 80–180 range, with median around 60.
- We do want streaming for longer transforms where tokens stream back progressively; for short prompts we prefer a low tail latency.

I'll populate the spreadsheet by EOD Wednesday (1/14) with the distributions and a separate sheet that lists a few representative prompt examples and expected token counts.

One ask: can Redwood indicate what a safe initial socket/connection pool size would be for the pilot (we'd like a starting point before you map the detailed profile)? If we can get a recommended pool size and an example burst window configuration, that will help our infra team configure the client side.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Lina
Director of Engineering
FastLane Inc

We can offer FastLane a pilot tier with an elevated burst allowance for the first 30 days: +20% on top of the standard rate limits for bursts (no extra charge), plus one-time credit of $2,000 to offset initial testing costs. This is contingent on the pilot being limited to the demo workload and us getting the filled spreadsheet.

Also, for the initial pool suggestion: recommend starting with a client-level connection pool of 250 sockets with multiplexing enabled and a server-side concurrency cap of 400 parallel requests for the pilot region (us-west). That gives headroom for the nightly peak while protecting throughput. We'll include an option to enable auto-burst (short 3-minute window) that can be toggled in the pilot config.

Lina / team —

Quick technical note from my side on graceful degradation and routing:

- Fallback model: if server-side parallelism hits the 400 cap, we can route excess requests to a lower-cost model variant with a higher tolerated latency (p95 < 900ms) until the burst subsides. This reduces error rates rather than queuing indefinitely.
- For streaming sessions, enable a separate slot allocation so long-lived streams don't occupy short-prompt concurrency. In practice we reserve 20% of cluster slots for streaming during the pilot window.
- Observability: we'll surface token-level latency histograms and per-connection utilization in the Redwood Console so your SREs can watch occupancy in real time.

I'll put these settings into a short JSON-like snippet and attach to the pilot doc (Karthik, I'll send that as soon as you add the SLO projection).

Cheers,
Ben

Redwood Inference
